findings.title: RSS-imported HTML is stored and served with no sanitization (raw_html cook method)
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], and Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim for that method, bypassing Discourse's entire markdown/sanitization pipeline. Any script/iframe/event-handler markup present in the RSS feed content (or in a page fetched by TopicRetriever/import_remote from the embeddable host) is stored as-is in `cooked` and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb line 19, and also on the main forum topic page. A compromised or malicious feed/embeddable site therefore gets stored XSS on the Discourse instance. The imported content must be sanitized (e.g. via Sanitize/Nokogiri whitelist) before storing.

findings.title: Unescaped URL interpolated into HTML in imported_from footer
findings.body:
`contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "` interpolates the raw feed item URL into an href attribute and link text with no HTML/attribute escaping. A feed entry whose link contains a single quote or angle brackets (e.g. `x' onclick='...`) injects arbitrary markup into the post body, which — combined with the raw_html cook path — is stored and served unsanitized. The URL must be escaped before being embedded in the HTML string.

findings.title: Weak origin check uses substring match on discourseUrl
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any origin that appears anywhere in the discourseUrl string. An attacker page at e.g. `http://evil.com/https://forum.example.com` or an origin like `http://forum.example.com.attacker.com` (which contains the forum origin as a substring) passes the check, and the handler then writes an attacker-controlled `e.data.height` into the iframe height. The check must compare parsed origins for equality, not substring containment.

findings.title: request.referer interpolated raw into inline JavaScript
findings.body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` interpolates the Referer header into a single-quoted JS string with no JS-string escaping. ERB's HTML escaping does not neutralize single quotes or backslashes inside a <script> block (entities are not decoded there), so a Referer such as `http://embeddable-host/'};alert(1);//` breaks out of the string and executes arbitrary script in the embed frame. Use a fixed targetOrigin (the Discourse base URL) or json_escape/j() the value.

findings.title: Feed polling has no error handling and retry disabled, so failures are silently swallowed
findings.body: Jobs::PollFeed sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` and `poll_feed` calls `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `TopicEmbed.import` for each item with no rescue. If the feed URL is temporarily down, returns malformed XML, or any item raises (e.g. `i.content` nil causing NoMethodError, or an invalid link), the exception propagates and the job dies without retry or notification; hourly polling then effectively stops working with no visibility. Exceptions should be caught/logged, and the whole job should not abort on a single bad item.

findings.title: Entire feed re-imported every hour; feed_key/dedup key defined but never used
findings.body: The `feed_key` method builds a redis key for the feed's last-modified state but is never called anywhere. Every hour the job iterates all feed items and runs TopicEmbed.import for each one, performing SHA1 comparisons and (when content changed) full post revisions for every historical item, forever. Feeds commonly keep hundreds of items, so this grows unboundedly. Use the feed's ETag/Last-Modified (the feed_key) or skip items whose URL was already imported.

findings.title: force: true added to an already-released migration will drop existing tables
findings.body: This PR modifies the previously shipped CreateTopTopics migration to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which drops any existing top_topics table before recreating it. On any deployed database where this migration is re-run (db:migrate:redo, restore-from-schema edge cases, or multi-site setups that replay migrations), all accumulated top_topics data is silently destroyed. `force: true` is only appropriate for development scratch tables, never for migrations against production data (same concern applies to the new create_topic_embeds migration, though that table is new).

findings.title: Import crashes if the embedded post was deleted
findings.body: In the update branch, `post = embed.post` may be nil if the topic's first post was deleted (the topic_embeds row is not cleaned up when posts are destroyed). The subsequent `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!` then raises NoMethodError, which in the poll feed job aborts processing of the entire feed. It should check `embed.post.blank?` and re-create or skip instead.

findings.title: import mutates the caller's contents string
findings.body: `contents << "..."` uses String#<< on the argument passed by the caller, permanently appending the 'Imported from' footer to the caller's string. In the poll feed loop this mutates local variables held by SimpleRSS items; if a caller reuses the string (e.g. logs it or compares it), it sees unexpected modifications. Use `contents = contents + ...` instead.

findings.title: Loading view reloads the iframe forever even when retrieval fails
findings.body: The loading page unconditionally reloads every 30 seconds. If the RetrieveTopic job failed (invalid embeddable host, fetch error, embed_by_username unset so TopicRetriever#fetch_http returns early), no TopicEmbed is ever created, and every visitor of the embedding page triggers an endless reload loop plus a new enqueued job per minute per visitor, generating continuous load on both the embedding site and the Discourse instance. The reload should be limited to a few attempts.

findings.title: Job requires irrelevant dependency 'email/sender'
findings.body: The RetrieveTopic job begins with `require_dependency 'email/sender'` although it has nothing to do with email; this appears to be copy-paste residue and loads unrelated mailer code in every sidekiq worker process running this job. It should require only 'topic_retriever'.
